A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, A Manifold Perspective on the Statistical Generalization of Graph Neural Networks. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F report original GNN experiments measuring generalization gaps, training/testing performance, and fitted relationships on node- and graph-classification datasets.

after.justification: V2 retains the original node- and graph-classification experiments in Section 5 and Appendix F, including measured performance and generalization-gap results.

M1.justification: The GNN/MNN architectures, graph constructions, training objectives, and prediction procedures remain unchanged. The revised filter assumptions and transport construction concern the theoretical analysis, without establishing an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight node-classification datasets and ModelNet10/ModelNet40 graph classification. No dataset, task, domain, or distinct testing scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Both versions study GNN/GCN width and depth variants, with no added or removed competing baseline method. The newly discussed manifold-learning methods are citations, not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F retain the reported sampling procedures, splits, metrics, optimization settings, training budgets, architecture sweeps, and linear-fit selection procedure. Changes to which train/test curves are displayed do not establish a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix width-sensitivity and overfitting evidence is reduced: separate train/test curves for 16- and 128-unit models disappear from the CS, Physics, Amazon, and Roman figure groups, although their generalization-gap curves remain. The new coefficient plot concerns the existing Arxiv fitting analysis, with no distinct robustness or ablation study.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 independent runs for node experiments and five random partitions for graph classification. The existing error-bar and mean/standard-deviation reporting practices remain; no new uncertainty estimation or statistical testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 and the main-text result curves are unchanged, but some appendix train/test curves have revised values or omitted model entries. New Figure 12 also reports coefficients inconsistent with retained Table 3: the two-layer, 64-unit Arxiv accuracy slope is plotted near -0.60, while the table gives -0.6301.

T1.justification: Equations 14 and 18 replace the difference of minimized risks with a supremum of absolute risk differences, and Definition 4 adds a derivative-decay condition. Appendix A replaces the equal-mass Voronoi construction with an optimal-transport partition; Appendices B–E revise spectral-error, Lipschitz, and risk-bound derivations. These substantially revise the mathematical foundation.

C1.justification: The introductory guarantee expressed through GA acquires a substantially different scope through its revised definitions: v1 compares separately optimized risks, whereas v2 claims uniform absolute empirical–manifold risk agreement over the parameter class, under stronger filter assumptions. The abstract and conclusion retain their wording and empirical claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix H argues that the low-pass assumption is mild, connecting high-frequency variation to instability and neighborhood homogeneity to low frequencies, with physical-model and PCA/Isomap analogies. V1 already imposed low-pass filters but lacked this substantive applicability argument.

D1.justification: Appendix F retains the same hardware, runtime estimates, dataset-access instructions, preprocessing/split disclosures, optimizer hyperparameters, epochs, batch sizes, dropout, and learning-rate scheduler details.

R1.justification: Appendix G adds positioning relative to manifold-hypothesis testing, dimension estimation, and manifold-learning methods. Appendix H adds citations supporting low-pass filtering, and the Voronoi-tessellation reference is removed. The principal positioning against earlier GNN generalization work remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. V2 makes localized setup and proof-explanation edits, relocates the inner-product definitions, expands Appendix G, and adds Appendix H; this is targeted revision rather than extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 12, enlarges axis and legend text in selected plots, simplifies several train/test panels, and redistributes appendix figures and tables. The Roman train/test panel remains on page 35 but loses its full figure caption. The overall visual organization is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical specificity through the transport partition and explicit derivative condition. However, support for the strengthened uniform-gap guarantee remains unclear because Appendix D still selects a population-risk minimizer, and new Figure 12 conflicts with unchanged Table 3. These theoretical gains and unresolved consistency problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
